target: UTM-bundled QEMU, HVF, one vCPU, VirtIO keyboard/tablet and WAV-backed virtio-sound-pci
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=build/psalmody-current-9a0d.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-current-psalmody-audio-9a0d.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-psalmody --probe-psalmody-audio-timer
verified: Psalmody launched, accepted recording and C-note input, played the note, and exited with Shift+Escape.
The WAV-backed VirtIO sound device captured 11,466 stereo frames at 44,100 Hz; 15,876 samples were nonzero and the peak amplitude was 7,000.
The strongest sustained tone measured about 516.8 Hz, consistent with the expected C5 note.
The experimental sound timer delivered 10 IRQs.
After exit, the graphical terminal evaluated 40+2 as 42 and zstatus reported failed=0.
scope_note: This verifies generated PCM and app interaction under UTM's bundled QEMU with a WAV sink. It does not verify audible playback through the live UTM window, all Psalmody editing workflows, or Pi hardware output.
